chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who marries a woman for temporary pleasure (mut'ah) and does not stipulate inheritance. He said: 'There is no inheritance between them, whether he stipulated it or did not stipulate it.'

Because this report is intended to mean what we previously mentioned, that it is the same whether he stipulated or did not stipulate, for she does not inherit, because there is no inheritance for her, and its establishment only requires a stipulation, not its removal. And that which indicates what we mentioned is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Does a wife in temporary marriage (mut'ah) automatically inherit from her husband?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that in temporary marriage (mut'ah), inheritance is not an inherent right but a contingent one, requiring explicit stipulation by the husband. The scholar notes that the absence of inheritance is the default state, meaning the condition serves to establish the right rather than merely preserve it, distinguishing it from permanent marriage where inheritance is automatic.
